page: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It features an AMD EPYC 4345P processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs via multi-threading at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 123.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding approximately 7.71 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with 3890 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The DDR5 memory subsystem achieves a top-tier Passmark memory score. However, multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scores falling into the average category. Additionally, memory write performance for large uncached blocks is a notable bottleneck, ranking in the bottom 25%, whereas read bandwidth remains average.

This hardware configuration offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that benefit from dedicated bare metal access without virtualization overhead. The combination of top-tier single-thread execution, fast DDR5 memory, and 3890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage makes this server well-suited for database operations, memory-bound applications, and lightweight LLM inference. It is also highly capable for static web serving and single-threaded data processing tasks, though highly parallelized multi-threaded workloads may be limited by its 8-core physical capacity.

The platform includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512.
